_why: ONE list of gates. The pre-push hook and .github/workflows/ used to keep two
hand-maintained lists, and nothing required them to agree. They stopped agreeing:
the hook ran asset-load-check against two URLs while CI ran it against every page,
so a green hook said nothing about the gate that was failing — and the Contrast gate
was red on thirty consecutive pushes from 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-04 while every local
Divergence is still allowed, because some sweeps are too slow for every push. What is
no longer allowed is UNDECLARED divergence: every gate names the stages it runs in,
and tools/run-gates.py --audit fails if a check exists that this file does not list.
stages : pre-push | ci     (a gate may be in both; at least one is required)
needs  : server            (run-gates starts ONE for all of them and passes {BASE})
stages : pre-push | ci | ci-always   (ci-always = canon-gate.yml, unfiltered)
serial : run this gate alone (virtual-time drivers break under contention)
cmd    : argv. {BASE} is substituted with the server origin.
runner:false = declared here, executed by the hook's own parallel orchestration.
The DECLARATION is single either way; --audit proves the hook really invokes it.

Two properties every other gate is blind to, because they compare elements to EACH OTHER instead of measuring one element: no two headings on a page say the same thing (o2 shipped its §01 stakes heading a second time over §04), and every section carrying its own h2 is reachable from the page's own jump nav (five of eight case studies had one that was not). Self-calibrates by planting a duplicate heading and by deleting a jump link. — stage 'ci', NOT 'ci-always': canon-gate.yml runs the ci-always stage with no Chrome and no pillow/websocket-client, because every other gate in it is pure text. Registering this browser-driven gate there turned the canon gate red on 5b92ef2c within minutes of the push — the gate could not start, which a workflow correctly reports as a failure.

Unit tests for contrast-audit's ink algebra — the only part of it that had none. Its correctness rests on four constants (ALPHA_CORE .7, ALPHA_FLOOR .5, CORE_BAND .10, DIFF_T 24), each set after a specific incident, and the ONLY verification was four end-to-end canaries on a live page: a browser, a server, a scroll loop and 12MB of screenshots to check arithmetic three lines long. Runs in milliseconds with no browser and no server, because it CONSTRUCTS the frames instead of photographing them — for ink I on ground G at coverage a, B=G, A=a*I+(1-a)*G, C=a*MAGENTA+(1-a)*G, which is exactly what the browser produces, so _measure cannot tell the difference and the expected answer is known in advance, which a live page can never give you. 17 assertions. The load-bearing ones: recovery is exact at full coverage; within 0.25 at ALPHA_CORE and 0.60 at ALPHA_FLOOR (the claim the floor rests on, previously untested); and BELOW the floor it returns UNMEASURABLE rather than convicting — that is the exact regime that produced ten false Linux failures, where #1A0D08 on #F67E99 (7.57:1) came back as #B1330C at 2.49:1, a colour in no stylesheet. A standing regression test now asserts that pair stays above 4.5 at four coverage levels. CALIBRATED by perturbation, not assumed: dropping ALPHA_FLOOR to 0.3 turns the below-floor assertion red, and removing the 1/alpha division turns the ALPHA_CORE recovery red. Restored bit-identical after both. It also corrected the v3 docstring, which conflates two invisibilities: ink==ground (frames A and B agree, but C still keys the glyph, so it grades 1.00:1 — a failure) and nothing-painted-at-all (no glyph in any frame — the real no-ink flag). My first version asserted the docstring and failed; the tool was right.

The pre-push hook invokes this through run-gates --only contrast-audit, so there is ONE command line. It previously spelled out its own and had drifted: --widths 1440 in the hook against 1440,390 in the manifest, with an exempt list two selectors shorter. runner:false is gone with it. — scoped: pre-push passes only the CHANGED pages (the hook falls back to every page when CSS, a partial or a tool changed). The full two-width sweep across all pages runs nightly. Only the page SET differs; widths, exemptions and force-visible come from this file either way. — --force-visible '.reveal' no longer describes anything on the SITE: the scroll-reveal was removed on 2026-09-07. It stays because canary C3 plants an element that hides itself and requires the pin machinery to surface it — PREP_JS SKIPS anything at opacity 0, and a skipped element is a silent pass. — OPEN 2026-09-05, AND STILL OPEN 2026-09-07: on a Linux runner this reports ten homepage failures that are NOT real. Every authored pair measures 6.4:1 to 10.7:1 from the stylesheet, and every ratio it reports is roughly half that — the signature of painted, partially-covered pixels being read as solid ink. It does not reproduce on macOS. Two attempted fixes did not clear it: an ALPHA_FLOOR guard (the alphas are above the floor) and a check comparing the recovered ink against the authored colour (too crude — it made 30 elements unmeasurable locally, because rgba() text and headings containing a gradient <em> are legitimately not their computed colour). RULED OUT SINCE: frame geometry (the camera calibration came back green on the runner, 16a07709) and the antialiasing-percentile bug (f3604213 graded the glyph core instead of its edge) — the nightly on 5b92ef2c reports the SAME ten. NEW EVIDENCE from that run's annotations, which are readable without auth at /actions/runs/<id>/jobs -> check_run_url + '/annotations': the recovered inks are not scattered, they CLUSTER ON VIOLET — #7E59FF, #885AFF, #8D5CFF, #7554FF against an authored #FF8A5C, and every one of those elements is a link, whose un-overridden token IS violet (--link). That is the signature of a CASCADE difference on the runner, not of noisy un-blend arithmetic: the .xi-* amber override winning locally and losing there. Next step is to dump the WINNING declaration for one of these anchors on the runner (getMatchedCSSRules order / stylesheet load order), not another alpha hypothesis. runner-diagnose.py and alpha-probe.py therefore STAY, and so does the tooling-budget ceiling they borrowed — the repayment recorded there is not due yet.

DIAGNOSED 2026-09-04 and returned to every-push CI: it was not a Linux defect and not a false positive — it was CPU contention between parallel virtual-time gates. MOVED OFF EVERY-PUSH 2026-09-04, UNEXPLAINED. Its CALIBRATION fails on the Linux runner — 'planted 19px Georgia CTA did not add a signature (selector matched nothing, or probe blind)' — and a gate whose calibration fails is correctly refusing to report. It calibrates fine on macOS. Same treatment and same open question as theme-remnant-check. — serial: this gate CALIBRATES BY WRITING INTO ember.css — a shared source file. Two such gates at once clobber each other's read-modify-write restore and leave a canary rule on disk permanently, which is how theme-remnant-check came to report #515863, its OWN plant, on 40 pages in CI. Reproduced locally by running three of them concurrently: two planted rules left behind and the same 40-page failure. The REAL fix is gatelib.planted(), which holds a lock across plant -> scan -> restore and does not depend on who schedules the gates; serial is belt-and-braces for a bug that corrupted the working tree.

Fix 04 from the architecture review, enforced rather than wished. tools/ is 1.98x the size of the site CSS it checks; the ceiling makes the next increase a decision someone records instead of a drift nobody notices. Raising CEILING is expected and fine — raising it silently is not.

WCAG 1.4.10 reflow at 320px and 2.5.8 target size at 24x24 — two AA requirements with no instrument in this repo before 2026-09-06. 320px is the actual requirement (1280px at 400% zoom, which is how a low-vision reader reads this site); every other gate here starts at 390, so reflow had never been measured. And the notes in this repo assumed 44px targets, which is SC 2.5.5 (AAA) and a different requirement, so the AA line was unchecked. Written on the cream branch and cherry-picked here because it is theme-agnostic.

In the page's DEFAULT, untouched state, no viewport-anchored element may cover the content. Written after an unscoped `display:flex` at #nav specificity outranked @media(max-width:1100px){.nav-links{display:none}} and left the mobile drawer PERMANENTLY OPEN below 1100px on every page — an opaque panel over the top 475px with pointer-events:auto, eating every click under it. It laid out correctly at 1200+, so both menu gates (which OPEN the menu before looking) passed it. Swept across a width RANGE, mobile first, because the defect hid between the widths anyone checks. Two calibration plants: a fixed cover that must fire and an absolute one that must not.

Compares two SIBLINGS to each other — the one thing no other gate here does. Arpit selected the homepage act numeral on 2026-09-08 and said the numerals do not align to their text. He was right in all four acts at every width: .chap used align-items:start, so the numeral and its title had IDENTICAL box tops (1141.0 and 1141.0) while their baselines sat 6.0px apart at 1440 and 7.0px at 768/390 — the numeral is solid-set (line-height:1), the title carries half-leading. Every gate passed it, and had to: contrast, overflow, spacing, reflow, leading, heading-rank and a11y each ask about ONE element's own properties or its place inside its own container. receipt-align-check was the only relative check and it tests LEFT edges of one component on six case pages. First sweep found four real defects beyond the reported one: footer .fresh carried a stacking margin into a flex row and sat 3.0px low on 34 pages; #thoughts .ixi and lab .dsg-type were centred where a baseline was wanted. Measures via a zero-size inline-block probe (the browser's own baseline) — NOT font arithmetic, which over-reported by 4px on a row the browser had already aligned exactly. ~110s for 59 pages x 3 widths; kept at all three because 390 is where layouts fail.

Prose that escaped its column. Arpit selected a homepage line on 2026-09-09: "why is this line jumping off the grid and why couldn't you catch it". I had moved that paragraph the same session and landed it as a SIBLING of .wrap rather than inside it, so it rendered 0..1440 where the column runs 140..1300 — and in the wrong section. Two causes: the move found its boundary with `.index('')` ("the next closing tag", which the execution lessons forbid), and the verification asked whether the string was PRESENT. Presence is not placement. Three premises failed before this one: (1) "every section has a .wrap" — five column containers exist by page family; (2) "a section's modal left edge IS its column" — /fit/ has three legitimate left edges; (3) "nothing legitimate spans >=90% of the viewport" — true at 1440, false at 390 where the column is 358 of 390px, which produced 53 findings ALL reading exactly 92%: an identical reading across 53 elements indicts the instrument. So it compares an element to its own section SIBLINGS instead, which needs no column and behaves the same at every width. BOTH sides is the discriminator: the envelope test alone gives 61 hits and every legitimate one escapes on exactly ONE side (a title flush-left in a padded card left+24/right+0, an indented quote left+0/right+27, a rail eyebrow left+253/right+0) — those are alignments. Escaping left AND right means it is not in the column at all: 61 hits become 0, while the real defect still shows 140px a side at 1440 and 16px at 390. Blind to a paragraph shifted sideways at the same width as its siblings. ~43s, 70 page-widths, plants the real defect shape at both widths before reporting.

Braces balance, and @layer still wraps the share of its file it used to. Written 2026-09-10 after ONE orphan `}` in ember.css closed @layer base at char 29,123 instead of 191,305 — dumping ~161KB, the bulk of the stylesheet, OUT of the layer. Unlayered rules outrank layered ones regardless of specificity, so the cascade for the whole site inverted on one character. The only visible symptom was a single homepage h2 at 44px instead of 42 (.voices h2, higher specificity, previously layered and losing, started beating body.p-home main h2); heading-rank-check caught that pixel and nothing looked at the cause, which was sitting in plain text. The brace arrived because a media query was moved by cutting to `c.index('}\n', ...)` — "the next closing brace", the CSS twin of "the next closing tag" that execution lesson 2 forbids by name, committed in the same session as a gate written about that mistake in HTML. Text only: no browser, no server, ~0.2s. It WOULD be cheap enough for pre-commit and I registered it with a "pre-commit" stage on 2026-09-10 — but run-gates only accepts pre-push/ci/ci-always/nightly and there is no .githooks/pre-commit at all, so nothing ever ran it there. A declared stage that no runner honours is a false claim; corrected to pre-push, which is where it actually runs. Adding a pre-commit hook is Arpit's call, not something to invent inside a gate registration. Comments are blanked first, so a `}` in prose cannot fool it. Calibrated against the real defect, not a toy: goes red with 3 findings including "@layer base wraps 8% of the file, baseline 57%". Read the layer-share line to localise it — the negative-depth line number lands at the layer's real closing brace, not the typo, because an orphan brace inside a layer legally closes it. Blind to whether the layer ASSIGNMENT is correct, only that it did not change.

WCAG 1.4.11: can a reader SEE a control, not just read it. Written 2026-09-10 after Arpit said of the calls to action "the cta are not very readable I am not sure how they are passing the accessibility test". They were passing because nothing looked: the CTA TEXT was fine (contrast-audit graded 347 text nodes on a case page, 0 failures) while the BUTTON'S BOUNDARY sat at 2.84:1 where 1.4.11 needs 3:1 — 29 of 38 asks. All 48 gates measured text against its ground; none measured a control's edge, so a button nobody could find passed every one of them. It ran MANUAL for one afternoon because it reported 153 controls across 17 components — the site's own tokens, not the CTAs: --border 1.41:1, --border-accent 2.89:1, and every card, input, toggle and Subscribe button inherited one. Arpit's call was to raise them site-wide, so the alphas were SOLVED for rather than guessed (ember --border .14 -> .37, --line .16 -> .37, --border-accent .5 -> .54, cream .2 -> .5, styles :root .07 -> .34, styles light .16 -> .49 and its accent .5 -> .75, the lab link outline 45% -> 58%). Now clean at 70 page-widths, so it is a regression guard. ONE reasoned exception: the .recon blocks are simulations of clients' shipped products (1.03:1 to 1.25:1) and are NOT raised — restyling them would falsify the evidence the case studies rest on. The check's own scope excludes them, and styles.css records why. Computes from RESOLVED COLOURS, never pixels. That rule cost SIX consecutive instrument faults, every one of them the probe and never the page: rounded corners read as 1.00:1; antialiased glyph edges read 1.47:1 against a 16.74:1 median; mobile emulation shifted the screenshot frame so every 390px reading was exactly 1.00:1; scrollIntoView returned a stale rect under smooth scrolling; sampling a button's centre hit its LABEL not its fill; and finally color-mix() resolves to color(srgb 0.9 0.4 1 / .45) whose channels are 0..1, which read as 8-bit turned a violet border into near-black and reported 21 visible links as failures. A gradient's endpoints ARE its extremes, so the worst case is exact. Semi-transparent borders are composited over the real ground — discarding them made it fall through to the card fill and report 1.15:1 for every card on the site. A boundary needs all FOUR sides: a bottom-only border is an underline, whose requirement is the text one. Native appearance:auto controls (53 checkboxes, 6 ranges) are reported UNMEASURABLE, not failed: the browser paints them and accent-color only touches the checked fill. --all lifts the action-family scope.

Reports 2 findings that were verified BY EYE on 2026-09-04 and are false positives: index.html and folio/index.html hero, and the 'who you'd be hiring' band, are staggered TWO-COLUMN compositions — prose left, the process film / Candidate Facts card right — and they render balanced at 1440 (prototypes/renders/hero-1440.png, chap-i-1440.png). The gate's unit is the paragraph: a column that starts BELOW the headline leaves the eyebrow and h1 with nothing level with them, so they read as one-sided. Widening the test to the section was tried and REJECTED — it let the gate's own planted 400px defect through, and a check that cannot fail is not evidence. Kept manual rather than weakened, so it never blocks CI on a reading a human has already overruled. Re-run it by hand after any layout change.
